# Offline regression evidence pipeline, contract 3.0

Repair and extend the provided H3Act project so `python3 main.py` compiles payloads,
replays decoded client events, and audits compressed origin captures. The existing
schema models, FuzzExecutor adapter, and HttpClient form the application, not an
external service. The offline clock is a socket-free coroutine utility. Complete
the byte-program and audit extension and repair integration/lifecycle defects.
Equivalent implementations are accepted; internal algorithms are your choice.

This model starts after transport delivery/field decoding. It sends no packets,
runs no model, and has no live CDN, QPACK, TLS, SSH, GPU, response cache, or wall-time
simulation. Its receipt encoding below is an audit format, not HTTP/3 wire format.
Diagnostic flags describe this paired recording, not a proof of a real exploit.

## Input and domain

Read exactly one UTF-8 JSON object without a byte-order mark, with surrounding
JSON whitespace allowed.
Reject duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8/JSON, nonfinite numbers (including overflowing
exponents), trailing values, wrong types, unknown/missing keys, or budget violations
with exactly `{"error":"input"}` and exit0. Every input string must encode as
UTF-8; lone Unicode surrogates are invalid. Booleans are not integers. No coercion.
Validate the whole input, including frames/events that ultimately are not used.
Otherwise output the result described below and exit0. Emit JSON only on stdout.

The root has exactly `seed`, `definitions`, `timeout_ms`, `cases`, `events`, `channels`.
`seed` is 0-64 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/dot/hyphen. `timeout_ms` is an integer
in [1,1000000000]. Names of cases/channels are unique within their kind and use
1-32 of those ASCII characters. Arrays preserve order. Object member order is
irrelevant except for the ordered header mapping described below.

Budgets are inclusive: raw stdin8MiB; definitions8192; cases2000; channels256;
combined number of case frames + external events + capture parts50000; combined
header pairs in input frames and external events32768; pairs per header block128;
expression source8192 Unicode code points; other template source65536 code points.
Logical byte sequence lengths, channel lengths, receipt lengths, body lengths,
and virtual times are in [0,2^63-1]. Every case's sum of pauses + timeout_ms must
fit this range. At most20000 complete origin requests and40000 complete chunk-size
lines (including zero chunks and lines in an unfinished request) may be examined
across all channels. Count a line in chunk-size position after its CRLF/line-limit
check and before checking the hexadecimal size or suffix; a malformed line
terminator or unfinished line is not counted. These are input-domain budgets, not a scoring objective.

Compressed captures cover very large objects and repeated boundary probes without
storing their expanded contents. Metadata counts model a batch audit between
experiment rounds; signed64-bit offsets permit sparse capture ranges. Resource
limits support an interactive batch audit and are not a speed ranking. Materialized
traffic volume or the number of discovered diagnostic flags is not a score.

## Byte expressions, templates and fingerprints

`definitions` is an ordered array of `[name, expression]`. Names are distinct,
non-keyword Python identifiers matching `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}`. An expression
can refer only to earlier definitions. The accepted Python expression syntax is:
Unicode string or bytes literals; nonnegative integer literals <=2^63-1; earlier names; parentheses;
concatenation `+` of byte sequences; repetition `*` with one byte sequence and one
integer (either order); and a byte slice `[lo:hi]` with either endpoint optionally
omitted. A final expression must be bytes, never an integer. Slice endpoints are
integer literals, with 0<=lo<=hi<=length; omitted endpoints mean0/length. No negative
index, nonempty slice step, integer arithmetic, boolean, call, attribute,
list, format string or other syntax is supported. AST nesting depth is at most128,
counting the root expression body as depth0 and every AST child edge, including
slice/operator/context nodes. Parentheses do not add AST depth.
Definition sources use CPython3.11 `ast.parse(source, mode="eval")` as supplied,
without whitespace normalization; sources it rejects are invalid. Empty third
slice components (`[lo:hi:]` or `[::]`) are equivalent to an omitted step.
Unicode string literals encode to UTF-8; bytes literals supply their exact bytes
before any byte operation; slices are byte offsets,
even within an encoded character. An empty sequence and zero repetitions are legal.

Every template is a JSON string. A string starting `{{` and ending `}}` is a whole
expression template: strip those outer markers and surrounding expression whitespace,
then evaluate it. Other strings are UTF-8 literal data, except each occurrence of
`<<random_string>>` is replaced by the first20 lowercase hex characters of SHA256
of the UTF-8 string `seed/coordinate/occurrence`. Occurrences are numbered from0
left to right independently per template. Tokens inside expression string literals
are literal data. Markers embedded in an ordinary literal are not expressions.
Coordinates are exactly:

- Frame j of case i: `case/i/frame/j/data`; header pair k uses
  `case/i/frame/j/h/k/n` for its name and `/v` for its value instead of `/n`.
- External event i: `event/i/data`, or `event/i/h/k/n` and `/v` for headers.
- Capture part j of channel i: `channel/i/part/j/data`.

All indices in coordinates use unpadded decimal. A fingerprint of bytes b is exactly
`{"n":N,"h":"hhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh"}`: N is byte length and h is the 16-digit lowercase
hex value of sum((b[i]+1)*257^(N-1-i)) modulo2^64. Empty bytes have n0 and all-zero h.
A fingerprint is a requested exact checksum; checksum equality is not asserted
to prove byte equality. Routing-identity comparisons below compare actual bytes.

## Cases, frames and external events

Each case is exactly `{"name":NAME,"frames":[FRAME,...],"expect":EXPECT}`.
EXPECT has exactly `method`, `target`, `host`: nonempty ASCII visible strings
(no whitespace), each at most8192 bytes; method is an HTTP token. This is supplied
intended routing identity for comparison, rather than a hidden inference target.
A token uses ASCII letters, digits and `!#$%&'*+-.^_` plus grave accent, `|~`.

Frames keep the project model names and spelling:

| Type | Input fields besides required Type |
| --- | --- |
| `headers` | Exactly one of `headers_kv` (string:string object) or `data_to_transfered` (array of two-string arrays); optional boolean `End_Stream`, default false |
| `data`, `datagram` | Required string `data_to_transfered`; optional boolean `End_Stream`, default true |
| `sleep` | Required integer `Time_to_Stop` in [0,2^63-1]; no End_Stream |

All other keys are forbidden. Header mapping pairs follow JSON member order; the
list representation also preserves duplicates. Compile each header name/value or
data string as a template. Do not validate HTTP field content in these fuzz frames:
malformed/duplicate pseudo fields are deliberately representable. A sleep consumes
virtual milliseconds, emits no frame and cannot finish a request. A datagram emits
a frame but its End_Stream is ignored. Headers/data with End_Stream=true close
the request send side. Any later non-sleep frame for that stream is a send error
and is not emitted; a sleep after request-end is still permitted.

All cases start at virtual time0, in case-array order, on one connection. Their
stream IDs are4*i. External events are exactly one of:

- `{"at":T,"kind":"headers","stream":S,"fields":[[name,value],...],"end":BOOL}`
- `{"at":T,"kind":"data","stream":S,"data":TEMPLATE,"end":BOOL}`
- `{"at":T,"kind":"close"}`

T is a nonnegative signed64-bit time, S is an integer in [0,2^32-1]. Compile all
event fields/data as templates. The event array may be out of timestamp order.
At equal time, ordering is: all initial case starts first; external events in
input-array order; pause completions in case-array order; timeouts in case-array
order. Frames between awaits are emitted together in source order. There is no
real sleep. A zero pause still yields to same-time external events.

Each case retains response events on its allocated stream until the first event
with end=true. Unknown streams, later response events, and events for an already
terminal case are ignored. Responses arriving while a case is still sending or
paused must be retained. A case is `ok` when both its frame sequence is exhausted
and a response end has been retained. It is `timeout` at send-finish+timeout_ms
if still awaiting response end; an exactly tied response event wins. A connection
close terminates every nonterminal case as `closed`, including paused senders,
and prevents later emissions. A later close cannot replace an already terminal
result. A send error makes the case `send_error`. State and completion time are
fixed at termination. Accepted response events before that termination remain in
its receipt even when the case closes/times out/errors. A response end alone does
not cancel remaining request frames or pauses.

## Client receipts and output case records

Each emitted action contributes this concatenation to its case's sent receipt:
8-byte big-endian unsigned virtual time,4-byte big-endian stream ID,one ASCII kind
byte,encoded content,and one final byte (1 for end,true;0 otherwise). Kinds are
`H` for sent headers, `D` for data, `G` for datagram. Datagram's final byte is0.
Header content is8-byte pair count,then for each pair:8-byte name length,name bytes,
8-byte value length,value bytes. Data content is8-byte data length followed by data.
Accepted received events use exactly the same format with lowercase `h`/`d`.
Receipts concatenate in their case's actual emission/acceptance order.

The result root is exactly `{"cases":[CASE_RECORD,...],"channels":[CHANNEL_RECORD,...]}`.
Case records follow input case order and have exactly:
`name`, `stream`, `state`, `at`, `frames`, `request_frames`, `payload_bytes`, `sent`,
`received`, `response_frames`, `response_body`, `origin_count`, `flags`.
`at` is completion time. frames counts emitted non-sleep actions; request_frames
counts emitted headers/data actions. payload_bytes sums header name/value lengths
and data/datagram lengths, excluding receipt framing. sent/received are fingerprints
of their receipts. response_frames counts accepted external headers/data events;
response_body fingerprints only accepted external DATA bytes in order.
Origin count and flags are defined below. All counts/offsets/times are JSON integers,
excluding booleans. No extra output keys, duplicate keys, nonfinite values, extra
JSON values or nonzero exit status are accepted. Object key order is free.

## Origin channels and request framing

Each channel is exactly `{"name":NAME,"parts":[{"case":OWNER,"data":TEMPLATE},...]}`.
OWNER is a case name or null. Parts concatenate in order; zero-length parts are
legal. Owners are recording provenance labels, not parsed Host/User-Agent fields.
Channels are independent byte streams. Parse consecutive HTTP/1.1 requests from
byte0. Fully framed requests contribute records; stop at the first syntax error
or unfinished request, retaining earlier records. Byte offsets are channel-relative
and half-open. A channel error is exactly `{"kind":"syntax"|"incomplete","offset":R}`,
where R is the start of the first uncommitted request. An empty/fully consumed
channel has error null.

Lines require CRLF, with at most8192 bytes before CRLF. If no LF has arrived and the remaining prefix has at most8193 bytes,
it is incomplete; line content is checked only when LF arrives. A bare LF or an LF beyond the line limit is syntax. A prefix
longer than8193 bytes without LF is syntax. A request line is exactly
`METHOD SP TARGET SP HTTP/1.1 CRLF`; METHOD is a nonempty token and TARGET is
nonempty ASCII visible bytes excluding SP. No alternate whitespace separator.

Header lines are `NAME:value CRLF`, followed by an empty line. NAME is an ASCII
token, case-insensitive for framing rules. Values allow SP..tilde and HTAB only;
strip outer SP/HTAB, preserve all interior bytes. No folding. Initial block size,
including request line and final empty line,is at most65536 bytes and128 fields.
Block size/count checks occur after each complete line; an unterminated line
is governed by the line-prefix rule above.

No Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding means zero body, regardless of method.
Every Content-Length occurrence contains a nonempty comma-separated list of decimal
unsigned values; trim SP/HTAB per member,permit leading zeros,and require all values
identical and <=2^63-1. A Transfer-Encoding is permitted only as one field with
trimmed case-insensitive value `chunked` and no Content-Length. Conflicts are syntax.
A length body is exactly the declared opaque bytes; bytes resembling requests do
not create new messages. Insufficient bytes mean incomplete.

Chunked bodies have hexadecimal unsigned size lines with optional `;` and an
uninterpreted suffix of SP..tilde/HTAB. No whitespace in the size,at least one hex
digit,leading zeros allowed,numeric value <=2^63-1. A nonzero chunk has exactly its
size in opaque bytes and then CRLF. A zero size is followed directly by a trailer
field block and final empty line. Trailer block size (excluding zero-size line)
is at most65536 bytes and128 fields; Host,Content-Length,Transfer-Encoding names
are forbidden there. Other duplicates are preserved. A missing body/suffix/trailer
is incomplete. A wrong complete suffix/line/field is syntax. Concatenate only
nonzero chunk DATA for the body fingerprint. Headers/trailers use the same field
rules. The parser's stated limits are this capture-reader policy,not a full HTTP
implementation or a claim that every tolerated request is RFC-conformant.

## Origin records and paired evidence flags

A channel record has exactly `name`, `bytes`, `requests`, `committed`, `error`.
bytes fingerprints the complete concatenated capture. committed contains the count
of complete published requests after each input part,including zero-length parts.
Requests follow byte order. A request record has exactly `start`, `end`, `method`,
`target`, `host`, `host_count`, `headers`, `body`, `trailers`, `framing`, `owner`,
`owners`, `flags`. Method/target are byte fingerprints. If exactly one Host exists,
host fingerprints its trimmed ASCII-lowercased value; otherwise it is empty.
headers/trailers fingerprint their field blocks encoded as8-byte pair count then
8-byte name length,name bytes,8-byte trimmed value length,value bytes per pair,
preserving name spelling and pair order. framing is `none`, `length`, or `chunked`.
body fingerprints the deframed opaque body.

owner is the provenance label of the request's first byte. owners is an array of
[label,positive byte count] for the complete raw request span,merging equal labels
and ordered by their first occurrence. Raw span includes framing,headers,trailers.
Request flags are a lexicographically sorted set:

- `unattributed`: owner is null.
- `mixed_owner`: some positive byte of the raw request has a different owner.
- `missing_host`/`multiple_host`: zero/more than one Host field (even identical).
- `identity`: a named owner has any mismatch against its expect: method/target
  compare exact bytes,Host must be unique and compares after ASCII case folding.
- `extra`: this is a named owner's second or later request in channel-array order,
  then byte order within each channel.
- `unsent`: named owner emitted no headers/data action,even if datagrams were sent.

origin_count per case counts requests whose first byte has that owner. Case flags
are sorted unique: `missing_origin` if request_frames>0 and count0; `extra_origin`
if count>1; `unsent_origin` if count>0 and request_frames0; `identity` if any owned
request has that flag; `mixed_origin` if any owned request has mixed_owner. These
flags never infer byte equality from checksums and do not label missing client
responses or legitimate origin expansion as vulnerabilities.

See RUNTIME.md for the complete public development and scored execution profiles.

## Local development wrapper (evidence infrastructure)


Local development uses a separate nonroot, chrooted outer process to run the
actual public checker or an opaque installation wrapper. Its limits are 120 s
wall time; 120/121 s soft/hard CPU per process; 2 GiB address space per process;
8 MiB stack; 128 file descriptors; process-count rlimit 64 per UID; 64 MiB per
file; and zero core dumps. The outer stdout/stderr caps are 16 MiB/1 MiB.
It uses the same published scratch path, reset, 0.25 s sampling, 1 GiB/50,000-entry
emergency policy, accounting limitations, and infrastructure-error/no-score
outcome described above. Network access is denied and CPU affinity is unchanged.

Ordinary process creation and same-UID child signaling are allowed in this outer
profile so the checker and opaque installer can launch, stop, and reap children.
Namespace creation remains forbidden: namespace clone flags are rejected,
unshare/setns are denied, and clone3 returns ENOSYS. These outer limits concern
local development evidence infrastructure and impose no candidate algorithm
requirement. Each scored translation invocation, including the public checker's
bounded translation child, continues to use the scored limits above and their
child/thread/signaling denials. The outer profile changes no input semantics,
output schema, serialization, scoring behavior, or submission interface.

## Runtime, resources, and files

Submit the complete project directory at `/workspace/project`, with `main.py` as
its CLI entry. Additional regular source/data files are allowed: the original tree
must have at most256 entries and8MiB total regular-file bytes. Count files and
subdirectories below the project root; exclude the root itself. No symbolic/hard links or special
files. Generated bytecode/cache files are ordinary extra entries and are allowed
within the same budgets. The verifier receives this project tree, not changes to
check.py or files outside it. The project may be reorganized freely and may use
CPython3.11.14 standard library and the provisioned Pydantic2.12.5 dependency set.
Run `cd /workspace/project && python3 -B main.py` with one JSON object on stdin.
The child working directory is the submitted project.
Runtime and restored project are read-only during verification; `/workspace/tmp`
is scratch. The public image installs all dependencies from its included pinned
wheels with no runtime downloads. Local no-Docker staging exposes the same packages
at `/opt/h3deps`; main.py contains the matching path bootstrap.
The public sanity checker runs in the current public workspace as the same image
user; it does not chroot its child, freeze source permissions, or attest the
original submission tree. The private local controller supplies those filesystem
protections for acceptance trials. The public checker needs only public workspace
files and runs a real child
with pipe stdin/stdout. Text I/O, `.buffer`, raw fd 0/1, `fileno`, and `fdopen` work.
An explicit `os._exit(0)` succeeds only if correct JSON bytes reached the pipe.
The checker refuses to launch candidates as root. The image's default user is
UID 1000. Local authoring trials additionally use a nonprivileged chroot worker.

### Scored translation process

Each candidate invocation processes one whole maximum batch. Wall limit is 60 s;
CPU soft/hard limits 20/21 s; address space 512 MiB; stack 8 MiB; 32 FDs; per-file logical size
64 MiB; core dumps disabled; process-count rlimit 64 per UID, with creation of
children and threads denied independently. No CPU affinity binding is applied.
Stdout cap is 16 MiB, stderr cap 1 MiB. Scratch is `/workspace/tmp`, cleared before
each invocation. At 0.25 s intervals the controller checks reachable scratch
files, summing max(logical size, allocated bytes), and directory entries: over
1 GiB or 50,000 entries triggers an infrastructure error without a score. This is
an emergency brake, not an exact storage quota; open-unlinked files and transient
usage are not fully accounted. No additional aggregate scratch quota is used for
local acceptance. There is no aggregate cgroup memory/CPU guarantee in local runs.

Linux x86-64 seccomp returns EPERM for the following syscalls: socket, socketpair,
connect, shmget, shmat, shmctl, semget, semop, semctl, semtimedop, msgget, msgsnd,
msgrcv, msgctl, kill, tkill, tgkill, ptrace, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev,
unshare, setns, mount, umount2, pivot_root, chroot, setsid, setpgid, setuid, setgid,
setreuid, setregid, setresuid, setresgid, setgroups, open_by_handle_at,
name_to_handle_at, bpf, keyctl, add_key, request_key, perf_event_open, userfaultfd,
io_uring_setup, io_uring_enter, io_uring_register, pidfd_getfd, fork, vfork, clone.
clone3 returns ENOSYS. Non-x86-64 or x32 syscall ABI kills the process.
Privileges cannot be gained (`no_new_privs`); no sockets or network are available.
Local chroot runs expose no procfs, tests, solutions, authoring, or host directory.
Public checks are sanity checks, not the private acceptance suite. Formal container
isolation and artifact transport validation remain infrastructure responsibilities.

Local development uses a separate nonroot, chrooted outer process to run the
actual public checker or an opaque installation wrapper. Its limits are 120 s
wall time; 120/121 s soft/hard CPU per process; 2 GiB address space per process;
8 MiB stack; 128 file descriptors; process-count rlimit 64 per UID; 64 MiB per
file; and zero core dumps. The outer stdout/stderr caps are 16 MiB/1 MiB.
It uses the same published scratch path, reset, 0.25 s sampling, 1 GiB/50,000-entry

outcome described above. Network access is denied and CPU affinity is unchanged.

profile so the checker and opaque installer can launch, stop, and reap children.

"""Public Linux x86-64 resource/syscall adapter. Invoked by check.py as nonroot."""
import ctypes
import os
import platform
import resource
import signal
import sys

# x86-64 syscall numbers, matching the public PROTOCOL.md deny list.
DENIED = [41,53,42,29,30,31,64,65,66,220,68,69,70,71,62,200,234,101,
          310,311,272,308,165,166,155,161,112,109,105,106,113,114,117,119,
          116,304,303,321,250,248,249,298,323,425,426,427,438,57,58,56]


class Filter(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [('code', ctypes.c_ushort), ('jt', ctypes.c_ubyte),
                ('jf', ctypes.c_ubyte), ('k', ctypes.c_uint)]


class Program(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [('len', ctypes.c_ushort), ('filter', ctypes.POINTER(Filter))]


def restrict():
    if os.geteuid() == 0 or platform.machine() != 'x86_64':
        raise RuntimeError('nonroot Linux x86-64 required')
    for what, limits in [(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (512*1024**2,)*2),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (20,21)),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE, (32,32)),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_NPROC, (64,64)),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (64*1024**2,)*2),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_STACK, (8*1024**2,)*2),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0,0))]:
        resource.setrlimit(what, limits)
    instructions = [(0x20,0,0,4), (0x15,1,0,0xc000003e), (0x06,0,0,0x80000000),
                    (0x20,0,0,0), (0x35,0,1,0x40000000), (0x06,0,0,0x80000000)]
    for number in DENIED:
        instructions.extend([(0x15,0,1,number),(0x06,0,0,0x50000 | 1)])
    instructions.extend([(0x15,0,1,435),(0x06,0,0,0x50000 | 38), (0x06,0,0,0x7fff0000)])
    filters = (Filter * len(instructions))(*(Filter(*x) for x in instructions))
    program = Program(len(instructions), filters)
    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
    if libc.prctl(4,0,0,0,0) or libc.prctl(38,1,0,0,0) or libc.prctl(22,2,ctypes.byref(program),0,0):
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(), 'seccomp setup failed')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    os.chdir(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(sys.argv[1])))
    restrict()
    signal.pthread_sigmask(signal.SIG_UNBLOCK, {signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT})
    os.execv(sys.executable, [sys.executable, '-B', sys.argv[1]])

"""Typed payload models for compiled fuzz frames.

The models keep the project frame names and spelling from the protocol table
(`headers`/`data`/`datagram`/`sleep`, `data_to_transfered`, `End_Stream`,

from typing import Dict, List, Literal, Optional, Tuple, Union

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from modules.byte_program import MAX, Seq


class CompiledPayload(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True, extra='forbid')


class H3HeaderFrame(CompiledPayload):
    Type: Literal["headers"] = Field("headers", description="Fixed value, 'headers'")
    headers_kv: Optional[Dict[str, Seq]] = Field(
        None, description="Optional header mapping in JSON member order")
    data_to_transfered: Optional[List[Tuple[Seq, Seq]]] = Field(
        None, description="Compiled header pairs preserving duplicates")
    End_Stream: bool = Field(False, description="Whether this frame closes the request send side")


class H3DataFrame(CompiledPayload):
    Type: Literal["data", "datagram"] = Field("data", description="usually 'data'")
    data_to_transfered: Seq = Field(..., description="Compiled opaque payload bytes")
    End_Stream: bool = Field(True, description="Ignored for datagrams")


class H3SleepFrame(CompiledPayload):
    Type: Literal["sleep"] = "sleep"
    Time_to_Stop: int = Field(0, ge=0, le=MAX, description="Virtual pause in milliseconds")


Frame = Union[H3HeaderFrame, H3DataFrame, H3SleepFrame]


class FuzzingPayload(CompiledPayload):
    test_cases: Dict[str, List[Frame]] = Field(
        ..., description="A collection of test cases keyed by case name")


def compile_cases(cases, context):
    """Compile validated case frames into the typed payload model."""
    data = {}
    for index, case in enumerate(cases):
        frames = []
        for position, frame in enumerate(case['frames']):
            kind = frame['Type']
            base = 'case/%d/frame/%d' % (index, position)
            if kind == 'headers':
                if 'headers_kv' in frame:
                    raw = list(frame['headers_kv'].items())
                else:
                    raw = frame['data_to_transfered']
                pairs = []
                for slot, (name, value) in enumerate(raw):
                    pairs.append((
                        context.template(name, '%s/h/%d/n' % (base, slot)),
                        context.template(value, '%s/h/%d/v' % (base, slot))))
                frames.append(H3HeaderFrame.model_construct(
                    Type='headers',
                    headers_kv=dict(pairs) if 'headers_kv' in frame else None,
                    data_to_transfered=pairs,
                    End_Stream=bool(frame.get('End_Stream', False))))
            elif kind in ('data', 'datagram'):
                frames.append(H3DataFrame.model_construct(
                    Type=kind,
                    data_to_transfered=context.template(
                        frame['data_to_transfered'], '%s/data' % base),
                    End_Stream=bool(frame.get('End_Stream', True))))
            elif kind == 'sleep':
                frames.append(H3SleepFrame.model_construct(
                    Type='sleep', Time_to_Stop=frame['Time_to_Stop']))
            else:
                raise ValueError('frame type')
        data[case['name']] = frames
    return FuzzingPayload.model_construct(test_cases=data)

"""Origin framing and evidence audit extension.

Builds the paired origin evidence for compiled capture channels: HTTP/1.1
request boundaries, body summaries, source-byte attribution and the paired
diagnostic flags that compare a named owner's request against its supplied
expect. Checksum equality is never treated as byte equality.
"""
import re

from modules.byte_program import Mixer, empty_fingerprint, fingerprint_bytes
from modules.capture import (BudgetExceeded, Capture, Counters, INCOMPLETE,
                             SYNTAX, parse_channel)

TOKEN = re.compile(rb"[!#$%&'*+.^_`|~0-9A-Za-z-]+\Z")

REQUEST_FLAGS = ('extra', 'identity', 'mixed_owner', 'missing_host',
                 'multiple_host', 'unattributed', 'unsent')


def audit_channels(channels, cases, client_records):
    """Audit compiled channels against case expectations.

    `channels` is a list of (name, [(owner, node), ...]); `cases` maps a case
    name to its compiled expectation; `client_records` maps a case name to the
    replay record. Returns the channel records and per-case origin evidence.
    """
    counters = Counters()
    channel_records = []
    origin = {name: {'count': 0, 'identity': False, 'mixed': False}
              for name in cases}
    seen = {}
    for name, parts in channels:
        capture = Capture(parts)
        raw_records, error = parse_channel(capture, counters)
        capture.reset_cursor()
        records = []
        for raw in raw_records:
            records.append(finish_record(capture, raw, cases, origin, seen,
                                         client_records))
        channel_records.append({
            'name': name,
            'bytes': capture.fingerprint(),
            'requests': records,
            'committed': committed_counts(parts, raw_records),
            'error': error,
        })
    return channel_records, origin


def committed_counts(parts, records):
    """Complete published requests after each input part, zero parts included."""
    ends = [record['end'] for record in records]
    cumulative = []
    total = 0
    for _, node in parts:
        total += node.length
        cumulative.append(total)
    from bisect import bisect_right
    return [bisect_right(ends, mark) for mark in cumulative]


def finish_record(capture, raw, cases, origin, seen, client_records):
    owner, owners = capture.attribute(raw['start'], raw['end'])
    flags = []
    mixed = len(owners) > 1
    if owner is None:
        flags.append('unattributed')
    if mixed:
        flags.append('mixed_owner')
    if raw['host_count'] == 0:
        flags.append('missing_host')
    elif raw['host_count'] > 1:
        flags.append('multiple_host')
    if owner is not None:
        expect = cases[owner]
        if (raw['method'] != expect['method']
                or raw['target'] != expect['target']
                or raw['host_count'] != 1
                or raw['host'] != expect['host']):
            flags.append('identity')
            origin[owner]['identity'] = True
        if seen.get(owner):
            flags.append('extra')
        seen[owner] = seen.get(owner, 0) + 1
        record = client_records.get(owner)
        if record is None or record['request_frames'] == 0:
            flags.append('unsent')
        origin[owner]['count'] += 1
        if mixed:
            origin[owner]['mixed'] = True
    flags.sort()
    return {
        'start': raw['start'],
        'end': raw['end'],
        'method': fingerprint_bytes(raw['method']),
        'target': fingerprint_bytes(raw['target']),
        'host': fingerprint_bytes(raw['host']),
        'host_count': raw['host_count'],
        'headers': raw['headers'],
        'body': raw['body'],
        'trailers': raw['trailers'],
        'framing': raw['framing'],
        'owner': owner,
        'owners': [[label, count] for label, count in owners],
        'flags': flags,
    }


def case_origin(name, origin, record):
    """origin_count and sorted unique case flags for one case."""
    evidence = origin.get(name, {'count': 0, 'identity': False, 'mixed': False})
    count = evidence['count']
    request_frames = record['request_frames'] if record is not None else 0
    flags = []
    if request_frames > 0 and count == 0:
        flags.append('missing_origin')
    if count > 1:
        flags.append('extra_origin')
    if count > 0 and request_frames == 0:
        flags.append('unsent_origin')
    if evidence['identity']:
        flags.append('identity')
    if evidence['mixed']:
        flags.append('mixed_origin')
    flags.sort()
    return count, flags

"""Independent expectations for the offline evidence pipeline (test authoring)."""
import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
import sys

def fp(b):
    if isinstance(b, str): b = b.encode('utf-8')
    n = len(b); h = 0
    for i, x in enumerate(b): h = (h*257 + x + 1) % (2**64)
    return {'n': n, 'h': '%016x' % h}

def rand_token(seed, coordinate, occurrence):
    return hashlib.sha256(f'{seed}/{coordinate}/{occurrence}'.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:20]

def action(at, stream, kind, data, end):
    out = at.to_bytes(8,'big') + stream.to_bytes(4,'big') + kind.encode()
    if kind in ('H','h'):
        out += len(data).to_bytes(8,'big')
        for n,v in data:
            out += len(n).to_bytes(8,'big') + n + len(v).to_bytes(8,'big') + v
    else:
        out += len(data).to_bytes(8,'big') + data
    out += b'\x01' if end else b'\x00'
    return out

def field_block(pairs):
    out = len(pairs).to_bytes(8,'big')
    for n,v in pairs:
        out += len(n).to_bytes(8,'big') + n + len(v).to_bytes(8,'big') + v

# H3Act offline evidence pipeline

Run `python3 -B main.py` with a single JSON document on stdin (no arguments).
Pydantic and its pinned dependencies are preinstalled; the `/opt/h3deps` path
bootstrap in `main.py` covers the local no-Docker staging image. See
`../PROTOCOL.md` for the input/output and timing contract and `../RUNTIME.md`
for the runtime, dependency and submission-tree limits.

The pipeline is fully offline: it sends no packets, runs no model and has no
live CDN, QPACK, TLS or wall-time simulation. Its receipt encoding is an audit
format, not HTTP/3 wire format.

## Layout

| Module | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `main.py` | stdin document validation, budgets, orchestration and JSON output |
| `schema.py` | typed pydantic payload models (`headers`/`data`/`datagram`/`sleep`) carrying compiled byte payloads |
| `modules/byte_program.py` | compressed byte sequences with cached length/hash, the byte-expression grammar, definition context and template compilation (including `<<random_string>>` coordinates) |
| `modules/clock.py` | socket-free coroutine clock; equal-time ordering is case starts, events, pause completions, timeouts |
| `modules/events.py` | decoded response event records |
| `HTTP3_Just_Send.py` | `HttpClient` request/event core: send-side framing, response retention and the ok/timeout/closed/send_error lifecycle |
| `modules/fuzz_adapter.py` | `FuzzExecutor` frame conversion, action receipt encoding and case records |
| `modules/capture.py` | piecewise capture stream (windowed reads, compressed range hashes) and the HTTP/1.1 origin framing reader |
| `modules/capture_audit.py` | origin records, provenance attribution and paired evidence flags |

## Notes on the implementation

* Byte sequences are immutable trees caching a logical length and the exact
  fingerprint hash, so compressed repetition/slicing is combined in logarithmic
  time and very large captures, bodies and receipts are never expanded. Only
  small line windows are materialised while reading a capture, and declared
  bodies are skipped by length arithmetic.
* Fingerprints are a requested checksum; routing identity and provenance always
  compare actual bytes.
* All published budgets (document sizes, combined frames/events/parts, header
  pairs, examined origin requests and chunk-size lines) are enforced as input
  validation.

"""Origin framing and evidence audit extension.

Builds the paired origin evidence for compiled capture channels: HTTP/1.1
request boundaries, body summaries, source-byte attribution and the paired
diagnostic flags that compare a named owner's request against its supplied
expect. Checksum equality is never treated as byte equality.
"""
import re

from modules.byte_program import fingerprint_bytes
from modules.capture import Capture, Counters, parse_channel

TOKEN = re.compile(rb"[!#$%&'*+.^_`|~0-9A-Za-z-]+\Z")

REQUEST_FLAGS = ('extra', 'identity', 'mixed_owner', 'missing_host',
                 'multiple_host', 'unattributed', 'unsent')


def audit_channels(channels, cases, client_records):
    """Audit compiled channels against case expectations.

    `channels` is a list of (name, [(owner, node), ...]); `cases` maps a case
    name to its compiled expectation; `client_records` maps a case name to the
    replay record. Returns the channel records and per-case origin evidence.
    """
    counters = Counters()
    channel_records = []
    origin = {name: {'count': 0, 'identity': False, 'mixed': False}
              for name in cases}
    seen = {}
    for name, parts in channels:
        capture = Capture(parts)
        raw_records, error = parse_channel(capture, counters)
        capture.reset_cursor()
        records = []
        for raw in raw_records:
            records.append(finish_record(capture, raw, cases, origin, seen,
                                         client_records))
        channel_records.append({
            'name': name,
            'bytes': capture.fingerprint(),
            'requests': records,
            'committed': committed_counts(parts, raw_records),
            'error': error,
        })
    return channel_records, origin


def committed_counts(parts, records):
    """Complete published requests after each input part, zero parts included."""
    ends = [record['end'] for record in records]
    cumulative = []
    total = 0
    for _, node in parts:
        total += node.length
        cumulative.append(total)
    from bisect import bisect_right
    return [bisect_right(ends, mark) for mark in cumulative]


def finish_record(capture, raw, cases, origin, seen, client_records):
    owner, owners = capture.attribute(raw['start'], raw['end'])
    flags = []
    mixed = len(owners) > 1
    if owner is None:
        flags.append('unattributed')
    if mixed:
        flags.append('mixed_owner')
    if raw['host_count'] == 0:
        flags.append('missing_host')
    elif raw['host_count'] > 1:
        flags.append('multiple_host')
    if owner is not None:
        expect = cases[owner]
        if (raw['method'] != expect['method']
                or raw['target'] != expect['target']
                or raw['host_count'] != 1
                or raw['host'] != expect['host']):
            flags.append('identity')
            origin[owner]['identity'] = True
        if seen.get(owner):
            flags.append('extra')
        seen[owner] = seen.get(owner, 0) + 1
        record = client_records.get(owner)
        if record is None or record['request_frames'] == 0:
            flags.append('unsent')
        origin[owner]['count'] += 1
        if mixed:
            origin[owner]['mixed'] = True
    flags.sort()
    return {
        'start': raw['start'],
        'end': raw['end'],
        'method': fingerprint_bytes(raw['method']),
        'target': fingerprint_bytes(raw['target']),
        'host': fingerprint_bytes(raw['host']),
        'host_count': raw['host_count'],
        'headers': raw['headers'],
        'body': raw['body'],
        'trailers': raw['trailers'],
        'framing': raw['framing'],
        'owner': owner,
        'owners': [[label, count] for label, count in owners],
        'flags': flags,
    }


def case_origin(name, origin, record):
    """origin_count and sorted unique case flags for one case."""
    evidence = origin.get(name, {'count': 0, 'identity': False, 'mixed': False})
    count = evidence['count']
    request_frames = record['request_frames'] if record is not None else 0
    flags = []
    if request_frames > 0 and count == 0:
        flags.append('missing_origin')
    if count > 1:
        flags.append('extra_origin')
    if count > 0 and request_frames == 0:
        flags.append('unsent_origin')
    if evidence['identity']:
        flags.append('identity')
    if evidence['mixed']:
        flags.append('mixed_origin')
    flags.sort()
    return count, flags

"""FuzzExecutor frame conversion and execution against an injected transport.

The adapter converts typed compiled payload models into the frame mapping the
client consumes, records every emitted action and accepted response event into
the exact receipt encoding, and produces the client half of the case records.
"""
from HTTP3_Just_Send import HttpClient
from modules.byte_program import Mixer, concat, literal, size
from modules.clock import Clock
from modules.events import HeadersReceived, DataReceived, ConnectionTerminated, SendError


def action_pieces(at, stream, kind, data, end=False):
    """Receipt contribution of one emitted action or accepted response event."""
    yield literal(at.to_bytes(8, 'big'))
    yield literal(stream.to_bytes(4, 'big'))
    yield literal(kind.encode('ascii'))
    if kind in ('H', 'h'):
        yield literal(len(data).to_bytes(8, 'big'))
        for name, value in data:
            yield literal(size(name).to_bytes(8, 'big'))
            yield name
            yield literal(size(value).to_bytes(8, 'big'))
            yield value
    else:
        yield literal(size(data).to_bytes(8, 'big'))
        yield data
    yield literal(b'\x01' if end else b'\x00')


def write_action(mixer, at, stream, kind, data, end=False):
    for piece in action_pieces(at, stream, kind, data, end):
        mixer.add(piece)


def encoded_action(at, stream, kind, data, end=False):
    """Whole receipt contribution as one compressed sequence."""
    node = None
    for piece in action_pieces(at, stream, kind, data, end):
        node = piece if node is None else concat(node, piece)
    return node


class OfflineTransport:
    """Records emitted actions and forwards decoded events to the client."""

    def __init__(self, clock, count):
        self.clock = clock
        self.next_stream = 0
        self.ended = set()
        self.count = count
        self.sent = [Mixer() for _ in range(count)]
        self.frames = [0] * count
        self.request_frames = [0] * count
        self.payload_bytes = [0] * count
        self.client = None

    def get_next_available_stream_id(self):
        stream = self.next_stream
        self.next_stream += 4
